headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-action risk: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest local/app content while Devin has broad cloud write and external integrations.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files, screenshots, and supported macOS app content, so Devin-generated artifacts could be pasted or surfaced into it and treated as instructions. Devin can emit content through GitHub/Slack/Notion/Jira integrations, creating a plausible bridge. No shared MCP or filesystem is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Devin output is copied into ChatGPT Desktop via files, screenshots, or app context
IF ChatGPT Desktop treats imported content as instruction-bearing text
mitigations: Use a strict delimiter/template for any copied Devin output
Disable app-context ingestion for untrusted artifacts
Review Devin outputs before pasting into ChatGPT Desktop
Keep instruction text separate from data files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Devin handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and writes to GitHub/Slack/Jira/Notion. That creates a default path for sensitive material to move from ChatGPT into Devin’s broader external integrations, with potential exfiltration beyond the original workspace.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop is given sensitive files, screenshots, or IDE content
IF Devin is connected to any write-enabled integration such as Slack, Jira, or Notion
mitigations: Do not pass secrets or regulated data from ChatGPT to Devin
Restrict Devin integrations to read-only where possible
Use redacted copies of files for cross-agent work
Audit outbound Devin actions before approval
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction on shared artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has shell, filesystem write, git modification, and broad network egress; ChatGPT Desktop can read files and interact with connected apps. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, Devin can mutate state while ChatGPT consumes it, and the profiles show no locking or coordination primitive. That makes write conflicts and race conditions likely in default collaborative use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or cloud workspace
IF Devin performs writes while ChatGPT Desktop reads the same files or app state
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Check git status before and after each handoff
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor with write scopes to GitHub, Slack, Linear, Jira, and Notion, so if it consumes ChatGPT Desktop output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into real actions. ChatGPT Desktop can produce code or file-derived analysis, but no verification gate is documented between them. The blast radius includes commits and external messages.
conditions: IF Devin uses ChatGPT Desktop output without independent verification
IF Devin is allowed to commit, message, or ticket based on that output
mitigations: Require human review before Devin acts on ChatGPT output
Ask Devin to cite source files before taking action
Use a checklist for any external write action
Limit Devin to draft-only mode for sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Devin stores and transmits source code, issue trackers, chat, and docs through third-party integrations. The profiles do not specify residency or retention alignment, so a mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because both are closed-source and the compliance path is undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-sensitive data is processed by both agents
IF their vendor retention or region settings differ
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in cross-agent workflows
Review vendor retention settings for both tools
Keep EU or PHI data out of Devin integrations
Document the data class allowed for each agent
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA and residency review
